name: TapTap CLI
description: TapTap developer-operations plugin, running the official taptap-cli you installed on this machine: sign-in, game creation, store-listing edits, package uploads, qualification, review and release, test plans, asset library. Credentials stay in the CLI; writes need confirmation.
whenToUse: Work in the TapTap developer backend: sign in, find IDs, create a game, edit store-listing fields and the main package, upload packages, fill qualification gaps, submit or withdraw a review, publish, manage test plans, search the asset library

list_tools.description: List the TapTap business operations this plugin can run. Without `category`, returns a category overview (names, operation counts, and the global execution rules); with `category`, returns every operation in that category with its risk level, parameter schema, use_when/avoid_when, and the category's RULES. Fixed categories: overview (account summary), auth (sign-in and credentials), shortcuts (end-to-end commands), service-tools (diagnostics, profile, schema lookup); the rest are per-domain dynamic categories (app, asset-library, developer, package-management, qualification, test-plan). Data querying is not offered, so download, impression, rating and order metrics do not appear in the catalog. Drill into a category before doing business in a domain for the first time.

/properties/category.description: Category name from the overview. Fixed categories are overview, auth, shortcuts and service-tools; dynamic categories are app, asset-library, developer, package-management, qualification and test-plan. Omit it to get the overview.

call_tool.description: Run one TapTap business operation. `name` comes from list_tools (for example 'app get-app-module', or a shortcut such as 'upload-apk' or 'auth login-start'). `developer_id` and `app_id` are scope fields passed directly (mapped to --dev-id / --app-id); every other business field must go into `data` as a JSON object; any key other than scope and data is a control flag, mirrored as --flag; positional arguments such as file paths go in the `_positional` array. Writes must be confirmed with the user first: preview with dry_run:true, then repeat the identical arguments with yes:true. A failed result carries an execution_state field: not_executed means nothing took effect and it is safe to correct and retry; unknown means a write may already have been applied, so verify the actual state before deciding whether to retry rather than simply re-running.

/properties/name.description: Operation name from list_tools, for example 'app get-app-module'.

/properties/args.description: Operation arguments as a JSON object. developer_id/app_id are scope fields passed directly (mapped to --dev-id/--app-id); every other business field must go in `data` (a JSON object); any key other than scope and data is a control flag, mirrored as --flag. Keys beginning with `_` are plugin controls and never become flags: `_positional` (array of positional arguments such as file paths), `_help` (show that command's --help), `_timeout_seconds` (per-call timeout in seconds, max 870, for long uploads). When unsure, drill into the category with list_tools first.
